commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /etc/claude-code/.claude/skills/openspec-apply-change

Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change.

**Store selection:** If the user names a store (a store is a standalone OpenSpec repo registered on this machine) or the work lives in one, run `openspec store list --json` to discover registered store ids, then pass `--store <id>` on the commands that read or write specs and changes (`new change`, `status`, `instructions`, `list`, `show`, `validate`, `archive`, `doctor`, `context`, `schemas`, `view`). Once selected, treat `--store <id>` as sticky for the rest of the workflow. Every unscoped example of those commands below is shorthand: before running it, append the flag. For example, run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json --store "<id>"`, not the unscoped form shown below. Other commands do not take the flag. Hints printed by commands already carry the flag; keep it on follow-ups. Without a store, commands act on the nearest local `openspec/` root.

**Project check:** These steps expect a project that already uses OpenSpec. Before the first step that writes anything (`new change`, `archive`, `sync specs`, or authoring an artifact file), confirm the project has a root: run `openspec list --json` (with `--store <id>` when a store is selected, since the store is then the root) and read `root`. A root object means the project is set up. `"root": null` means it is not - there is no `openspec/` directory here, and a write such as `openspec new change` would create one as a side effect. The command also exits non-zero, which is that answer rather than a broken CLI, so read the JSON instead of retrying or working around it.

One `"root": null` is not about setup: when a `status` error message starts with `Declared in` or `Invalid store declaration in` and names this project's `openspec/config.yaml` (or `config.yml`), the project does use OpenSpec through a store it declares, which this machine cannot resolve (the store is not registered, or the `store:` line is malformed). Do not treat it as uninitialized and skip the branches below: stop before writing and show the user that error's `message` and `fix`.

Otherwise, with no root, what happens next depends on how this workflow was reached:

- **Auto-selected**: you chose this workflow yourself, without the user naming OpenSpec, naming this skill, or running its slash command. Stop using OpenSpec and answer the request normally, as you would with no OpenSpec installed. Do not ask them to set anything up and do not mention OpenSpec setup.
- **Explicit OpenSpec request**: the user named OpenSpec, named this skill, or ran its slash command. Stop before writing and ask how to proceed: set this project up (`openspec init`), target a store they already have (`--store <id>`), or continue without OpenSpec for this request. Wait for their answer.

In both branches, never create the root as a side effect: do not run `openspec init` until the user asks for it, do not hand-create `openspec/` files, and do not let a command create it.

**Input**: Optionally specify a change name (e.g., `/opsx:apply add-auth`). If omitted, check if it can be inferred from conversation context. If vague or ambiguous you MUST prompt for available changes.

**Steps**

1. **Select the change**

   If a name is provided, use it. Otherwise:
   - Infer from conversation context if the user mentioned a change
   - Auto-select if only one active change exists
   - If ambiguous, run `openspec list --json` to get available changes and ask the user to select one

   Always announce: "Using change: <name>" and how to override (e.g., `/opsx:apply <other>`).

2. **Check status to understand the schema**
   ```bash
   openspec status --change "<name>" --json
   ```
   Parse the JSON to understand:
   - `schemaName`: The workflow being used (e.g., "spec-driven")
   - `planningHome`, `changeRoot`, and `actionContext`: planning scope and edit constraints
   - Which artifact contains the tasks (typically "tasks" for spec-driven, check status for others)

3. **Get apply instructions**

   ```bash
   openspec instructions apply --change "<name>" --json
   ```

   This returns:
   - `contextFiles`: artifact ID -> array of concrete file paths (varies by schema - could be proposal/specs/design/tasks or spec/tests/implementation/docs)
   - Progress (total, complete, remaining)
   - Task list with status, source path, and source line
   - Dynamic instruction based on current state
   - Optional `context`: current required project instruction input from the selected root
   - Optional `operationGuidance`: current advisory guidance for apply
   - `missingArtifacts` (when present): required artifact ids with no output

   **Handle states:**
   - If `state: "blocked"`: show the message and pause implementation.
     - If `missingArtifacts` is non-empty: suggest completing the missing artifacts. Run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json`, select the next `ready` artifact (not `skipped` or `blocked`), and use `openspec instructions "<artifact-id>" --change "<name>" --json` for its rules and template. Keep the selected `--store <id>` on both commands.
     - Otherwise, follow the CLI instruction to create or repair the schema-configured tracking file from existing planning artifacts. Do not assume another artifact is ready or start implementation while blocked.
   - If `state: "all_done"`: report that all tracked tasks are complete and suggest review or verification as appropriate before archiving
   - Otherwise: proceed to implementation

   Treat `context` as a required prompt-level input. Read and consider it, and
   apply relevant project facts, conventions, and constraints while implementing.
   Treat `operationGuidance` as optional additive advice. Read and consider every
   entry, and follow entries that are applicable and compatible with the built-in
   workflow.

   Keep both fields separate from CLI-returned state, missing artifacts, tasks,
   progress, `contextFiles`, and the built-in `instruction`. They are not
   evidence of task completion, do not replace the built-in instruction, and do
   not permit bypassing a blocked state. If context conflicts with the built-in
   instruction, an explicit user choice, or a CLI-controlled value, report the
   conflict and preserve the controlling value. If guidance is inapplicable or
   conflicts with those controlling inputs, do not follow it and explain why.
   These are prompt-level behavior contracts, not enforceable checks.

4. **Read context files**

   Read every file path listed under `contextFiles` from the apply instructions output.
   The files depend on the schema being used:
   - **spec-driven**: proposal, specs, design, tasks
   - Other schemas: follow the contextFiles from CLI output

   Do not copy `context` or `operationGuidance` verbatim into implementation
   files or planning artifacts unless the user separately asks for that content.

5. **Show current progress**

   Display:
   - Schema being used
   - Progress: "N/M tasks complete"
   - Remaining tasks overview
   - Dynamic instruction from CLI

6. **Implement tasks (loop until done or blocked)**

   For each pending task:
   - Show which task is being worked on
   - Make the code changes required
   - Keep changes minimal and focused
   - Before editing, confirm the checkbox at the returned `sourcePath` and `line` still matches the task description; if it does not, rerun the apply instructions and use the refreshed location
   - Mark the task complete at its returned `sourcePath` and `line`: `- [ ]` → `- [x]`
   - Rerun the apply instructions and confirm that task is now done and progress changed
   - Continue to next task

   **Pause if:**
   - Task is unclear → ask for clarification
   - Implementation reveals a design issue → suggest updating artifacts
   - A task needs work beyond what the spec and tasks describe, or you are tempted to drop, narrow, defer, or accept exceptions to specified behavior to make it fit → surface the added scope and ask; do not absorb it silently
   - Error or blocker encountered → report and wait for guidance
   - User interrupts

7. **On completion or pause, show status**

   Display:
   - Tasks completed this session
   - Overall progress: "N/M tasks complete"
   - If all done: report that tracked tasks are complete and suggest review or verification as appropriate before archiving
   - If paused: explain why and wait for guidance

**Output During Implementation**

```
## Implementing: <change-name> (schema: <schema-name>)

Working on task 3/7: <task description>
[...implementation happening...]
✓ Task complete

Working on task 4/7: <task description>
[...implementation happening...]
✓ Task complete
```

**Output On Completion**

```
## Implementation Complete

**Change:** <change-name>
**Schema:** <schema-name>
**Progress:** 7/7 tasks complete ✓

### Completed This Session
- [x] Task 1
- [x] Task 2
...

All tracked tasks are complete. Review or verify the change as appropriate
before archiving. You can archive this change with `/opsx:archive`.
```

**Output On Pause (Issue Encountered)**

```
## Implementation Paused

**Change:** <change-name>
**Schema:** <schema-name>
**Progress:** 4/7 tasks complete

### Issue Encountered
<description of the issue>

**Options:**
1. <option 1>
2. <option 2>
3. Other approach

What would you like to do?
```

**Guardrails**
- Keep going through tasks until done or blocked
- Always read context files before starting (from the apply instructions output)
- If task is ambiguous, pause and ask before implementing
- If implementation reveals issues, pause and suggest artifact updates
- Keep code changes minimal and scoped to each task
- Update task checkbox immediately after completing each task
- Pause on errors, blockers, or unclear requirements - don't guess
- When a task needs work beyond what the spec describes, surface the added scope and pause - never silently narrow, defer, or simplify away specified behavior
- Only mark a task `- [x]` when its specified behavior is fully implemented, not when it is partially done or deferred
- Use contextFiles from CLI output, don't assume specific file names
- Use each task's sourcePath and line to update its exact checkbox
- Do not use context or operation guidance as proof that a task is complete
- Apply relevant project context; report conflicts with controlling workflow inputs
- Consider every guidance entry; explain any inapplicable or conflicting advice
- Do not copy runtime context or operation guidance into implementation files or planning artifacts
- Preserve CLI-controlled blocked/ready/all-done behavior and completion criteria

**Fluid Workflow Integration**

This skill supports the "actions on a change" model:

- **Can be invoked anytime**: Before all artifacts are done (if tasks exist), after partial implementation, interleaved with other actions
- **Allows artifact updates**: If implementation reveals design issues, suggest updating artifacts - not phase-locked, work fluidly

1	# Proposal
2	
3	## Why
4	
5	Reception has no place to record the microchip number implanted in a pet (F1 in `decisions.md`). PC-301 adds that one field to the pet record so it can be entered, corrected and seen. Looking a pet up by its microchip number is a separate ticket (D5).
6	
7	## What Changes
8	
9	- A pet gets an optional **microchip number** on both the add form and the edit form (D2, D7).
10	- Before validation, the entered value is trimmed and its spaces are removed. After that it must be exactly 15 digits, or the form shows the error "must be 15 digits". Only the digits are stored. Dashes, dots and other characters are not removed. The country and manufacturer code is not checked (D3, D9, D10, D15).
11	- A microchip number is unique across all pets of all owners. A duplicate gets "is already in use" and nothing more: no other pet or owner is named (D4, D10, D11). A pet never conflicts with its own number (D14).
12	- A malformed number gets the format error only, and a well-formed duplicate gets the duplicate error only. Either error is reported together with the form's other errors (D17).
13	- The edit form shows the stored microchip number. An empty field on the edit form removes the stored number (D8).
14	- The owner's page shows a "Microchip number" label and the pet's microchip number with each pet's other details. A pet without a number shows the label with an empty value (D6, D16).
15	- H2, MySQL and Postgres each get a named unique constraint on the microchip number. A duplicate caught by the database is reported as "is already in use" on the microchip number field (D12), through a `PetValidator` method that the controller's `catch` calls (D19).
16	- No seeded pet gets a microchip number (F8).
17	- Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are migrated by one script per database. The script adds the nullable column, then the unique constraint. The change documents the deployment and rollback steps in order (D23).
18	- The change ships in two releases (D25, which amends D23). On MySQL the code before this change cannot start against the migrated table, because its `data.sql` inserts pets by position and runs at every start (F12). Release 1 ships only the column lists for the pet inserts in `data.sql` (H2 and MySQL). Then the migration script runs. Then release 2 ships the microchip number. Rollback from release 2 redeploys release 1, which works on the migrated table.
19	
20	Not in this change: looking up a pet by its microchip number (D5), the microchip number on the visit form (D24), and the unnamed MySQL owner-and-pet-name constraint (D13, F4). The lookup ticket takes the visit form; the MySQL constraint needs its own ticket.
21	
22	Known gaps: PetClinic has no migration tool, so the scripts are applied by hand; and the tests of the migration scripts run only where Docker is available (D23).
23	
24	Accepted limitation: until the lookup ticket, a microchip number typed onto the wrong pet blocks the right pet, and reception cannot see which pet holds it (D22).
25	
26	## Capabilities
27	
28	### New Capabilities
29	
30	- `owner-details`: what the owner's page shows about the owner's pets. This change introduces it with the microchip number display (D6, D16). Existing display behaviour (name, birth date, type, F7) is not specified yet.
31	
32	### Modified Capabilities
33	
34	- `pets`: adds the microchip number rules for the add and edit forms (optional, format, uniqueness, own number, clearing, error reporting, duplicates caught by the database), plus the edit form showing the stored number. Two baseline requirements are modified:
35	  - "Duplicate names caught by the database": its scenario "Another integrity violation" now covers only violations that name neither the owner-and-pet-name constraint nor the microchip number constraint, because a microchip number violation shows the form again (D12).
36	  - "Validation errors are reported together": it now includes an error on the microchip number, with two new scenarios (D17).
37	
38	  The other baseline requirements are unchanged. The baseline's Purpose excludes the GET forms. The requirement that the edit form shows the stored number is a GET-form behaviour, so the Purpose needs a one-line update when this change is archived (see `tasks.md`, Workflow follow-up).
39	
40	## Impact
41	
42	- **Data**: a new nullable `microchip_number` column and a named unique constraint on the `pets` table in `db/h2/schema.sql`, `db/mysql/schema.sql` and `db/postgres/schema.sql`. The H2 and MySQL `data.sql` pet inserts get a column list in release 1, because they insert by position today (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`) and would not match a sixth column (D25). No seeded pet gets a number (F8). The Postgres `data.sql` already names its columns (`db/postgres/data.sql:36-48`) and is unchanged. Two new migration scripts, one for MySQL and one for Postgres, bring an existing `pets` table to the new schema (D23). H2 needs none: it is in memory.
43	- **Code**: `Pet` (new field), `PetValidator` (format and uniqueness checks, plus a lookup it does not have today, F6, and a method that rejects the field for a duplicate caught by the database, D19), `PetController` (passes the lookup to the validator, copies the field on edit, calls the validator's method when the new constraint is violated), and a new repository query for pets.
44	- **Views**: `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html` and `owners/ownerDetails.html`.
45	- **Messages**: a new message key for "must be 15 digits" and one for the "Microchip number" label, in `messages.properties` and every locale file that `I18nPropertiesSyncTest` checks. "is already in use" already exists (`messages.properties:4`).
46	- **Tests**: the `@WebMvcTest` suites for `PetController` need the new repository as a mock. `PetValidatorTests` builds the validator with no arguments (`PetValidatorTests.java:59`), so it has to change too. One new test on H2 adds, edits and clears a microchip number through the forms (D21). Another saves two pets with the same microchip number on H2, past the validator, and checks that the error names the constraint. A migration test per database runs each script against a `pets` table in the old schema; it needs Docker and is skipped without it (D23). The migration tests follow the existing MySQL and Postgres integration tests and add no dependency (D26).
47

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `owner-details`: what the owner's page shows about the owner's pets. This change introduces it with the microchip number display (D6, D16). Existing display behaviour (name, birth date, type, F7) is not specified yet.

### Modified Capabilities

- `pets`: adds the microchip number rules for the add and edit forms (optional, format, uniqueness, own number, clearing, error reporting, duplicates caught by the database), plus the edit form showing the stored number. Two baseline requirements are modified:
  - "Duplicate names caught by the database": its scenario "Another integrity violation" now covers only violations that name neither the owner-and-pet-name constraint nor the microchip number constraint, because a microchip number violation shows the form again (D12).
  - "Validation errors are reported together": it now includes an error on the microchip number, with two new scenarios (D17).

  The other baseline requirements are unchanged. The baseline's Purpose excludes the GET forms. The requirement that the edit form shows the stored number is a GET-form behaviour, so the Purpose needs a one-line update when this change is archived (see `tasks.md`, Workflow follow-up).

## Impact

- **Data**: a new nullable `microchip_number` column and a named unique constraint on the `pets` table in `db/h2/schema.sql`, `db/mysql/schema.sql` and `db/postgres/schema.sql`. The H2 and MySQL `data.sql` pet inserts get a column list in release 1, because they insert by position today (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`) and would not match a sixth column (D25). No seeded pet gets a number (F8). The Postgres `data.sql` already names its columns (`db/postgres/data.sql:36-48`) and is unchanged. Two new migration scripts, one for MySQL and one for Postgres, bring an existing `pets` table to the new schema (D23). H2 needs none: it is in memory.
- **Code**: `Pet` (new field), `PetValidator` (format and uniqueness checks, plus a lookup it does not have today, F6, and a method that rejects the field for a duplicate caught by the database, D19), `PetController` (passes the lookup to the validator, copies the field on edit, calls the validator's method when the new constraint is violated), and a new repository query for pets.
- **Views**: `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html` and `owners/ownerDetails.html`.
- **Messages**: a new message key for "must be 15 digits" and one for the "Microchip number" label, in `messages.properties` and every locale file that `I18nPropertiesSyncTest` checks. "is already in use" already exists (`messages.properties:4`).
- **Tests**: the `@WebMvcTest` suites for `PetController` need the new repository as a mock. `PetValidatorTests` builds the validator with no arguments (`PetValidatorTests.java:59`), so it has to change too. One new test on H2 adds, edits and clears a microchip number through the forms (D21). Another saves two pets with the same microchip number on H2, past the validator, and checks that the error names the constraint. A migration test per database runs each script against a `pets` table in the old schema; it needs Docker and is skipped without it (D23). The migration tests follow the existing MySQL and Postgres integration tests and add no dependency (D26).

118	
119	1. Deploy release 1, and make sure no instance of the code before it is still running or can be restarted.

122	
123	Rollback from release 2, in order:
124

The `catch` itself is covered with mocked messages (task 4.1).

139	- **Known gaps** (D23): PetClinic has no migration tool, so the scripts are applied by hand and nothing records whether a database has been migrated. 140	- [The validator now issues one query per submission that has a microchip number] → It is an indexed `exists` query on the unique constraint, so the cost is negligible.
141	- [Translations into nine languages may be poor] → The sync test checks only that the keys are present. Translations should be reviewed by a speaker before release, as for any new label.
142	- [A microchip number typed onto the wrong pet blocks the right pet, and reception cannot see which pet holds it] → Accepted until the lookup ticket (D22, following from D5 and D11).

- `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html` gets a text input for `microchipNumber` through the existing `inputField` fragment, after the birth date. `th:field` fills it with the stored value on edit (spec: "The edit form shows the stored microchip number").
- `owners/ownerDetails.html` gets `<dt th:text="#{microchipNumber}">` and `<dd th:text="${pet.microchipNumber}">` after the type (`ownerDetails.html:55-56`). A `null` renders as an empty `dd` (INFERRED Thymeleaf behaviour), which is what D16 asks for.

### 8. Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are migrated by one script each

Per D23, which replaces D20, as amended by D25. On an existing database, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pets` is skipped (`db/mysql/schema.sql:38`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:36`, VERIFIED), so the new column would never be created there. `spring.sql.init.mode=always` (`application-mysql.properties:7`, `application-postgres.properties:7`, VERIFIED) runs `schema.sql` on every start, so release 2 would meet a table without the column (review R1; the exact failure is INFERRED, not run).

The scripts:

- `db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN microchip_number VARCHAR(15) NULL`, then `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT unique_pet_microchip_number UNIQUE (microchip_number)`.
- `db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS microchip_number TEXT`, then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number ON pets (microchip_number)`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).
- None for H2: it is in memory and rebuilt on every start.

Column types and the constraint name match Decisions 1 and 5. The scripts sit under `src/main/resources/db/<database>/` but are not run at start: `spring.sql.init` reads only `schema.sql` and `data.sql` there (`application.properties:3-4`, VERIFIED). The `schema.sql` files still create the column and the constraint for new databases (task 1.1). Each script starts with a comment that says to run it after release 1 is deployed and before release 2 is (D25).

The change ships in two releases (D25, which amends D23). D23 said the old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column. On MySQL that is false: the old `db/mysql/data.sql` inserts pets by position with five values (`db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`, VERIFIED) and runs at every start (`application-mysql.properties:7`, VERIFIED), so the old code cannot start against a six-column table (review R1; the exact MySQL error is INFERRED, not run). It holds from release 1 on, because release 1 names the columns.

- **Release 1** ships only the column lists for the pet inserts in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql` (task 0.1). Nothing else changes. With a column list, the inserts work on the old table and on the migrated one, where the nullable `microchip_number` is left `NULL` (INFERRED, not run). The Postgres `data.sql` already names its columns (`db/postgres/data.sql:36-48`, VERIFIED), so release 1 changes nothing for Postgres.
- **Release 2** ships the microchip number: everything else in this change, including the migration scripts (tasks 1.1 to 5.1).

Deployment, in order:

1. Deploy release 1, and make sure no instance of the code before it is still running or can be restarted.
2. Run the script for the database against the existing database, while release 1 is still running. Release 1 keeps working against the new table, because its seed inserts name their columns and the rest of it never names the new column (D25).
3. Deploy release 2. Its `schema.sql` skips `CREATE TABLE`, and on Postgres the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number` finds the index the script made (INFERRED; task 1.5 checks it).

Rollback from release 2, in order:

1. Redeploy release 1. It works on the migrated table (D25). Do not redeploy the code before release 1: on MySQL it cannot start against the migrated table.
2. Leave the column and the constraint in place. Dropping them is a separate, later step, not part of this change.

The change stays one OpenSpec change; the two releases are ordered steps here and in `tasks.md` (D25).

*Alternative rejected:* a migration tool such as Flyway or Liquibase. A real team would use one, but PetClinic has none (known gap, D23).

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Existing MySQL or Postgres databases keep their old `pets` table, because `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` skips it] → The migration scripts of Decision 8 add the column and the constraint after release 1 and before release 2 is deployed (D23, D25). H2 is in memory and rebuilt on every start.
- [Release 2 is deployed before the migration script has run] → The steps in Decision 8 put the script before release 2. Nothing in the app enforces the order, because PetClinic has no migration tool (known gap, D23).
- [The H2 and MySQL seed inserts give values by position (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`), so they would not match a sixth column, and on MySQL the code before release 1 cannot start against the migrated table (F12)] → Release 1 gives them a column list before the script runs (task 0.1, D25). Rollback goes to release 1, never to the code before it. No seeded pet gets a number (F8).
- [Each database words its duplicate-key message differently, and H2 may put the name in upper case inside a generated index name] → The match ignores case and looks for the constraint name as a substring. Task 1.4 checks the real message on H2: it saves two pets with the same number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so the validator does not run, and asserts that the `DataIntegrityViolationException` names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. The race test (task 4.2) does not check the real message. If one request commits before the other's `exists` query runs, the validator rejects the loser and the `catch` never runs, and the page looks the same either way. The `catch` itself is covered with mocked messages (task 4.1).
- **Known gap** (recorded with D20; D23 does not change it): the duplicate is not tested through the forms on MySQL or Postgres. Their integration tests run only with Docker (`MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43`, `PostgresIntegrationTests.java:67-68`), and they do not exercise the microchip constraint. This is left as it is.
- **Known gaps** (D23): PetClinic has no migration tool, so the scripts are applied by hand and nothing records whether a database has been migrated. The migration tests (task 1.5) run only with Docker; without it they are skipped, and must be reported as not run rather than as passed. They add no dependency: they follow the existing `MySqlIntegrationTests` and `PostgresIntegrationTests` (D26, F13).
- [The validator now issues one query per submission that has a microchip number] → It is an indexed `exists` query on the unique constraint, so the cost is negligible.
- [Translations into nine languages may be poor] → The sync test checks only that the keys are present. Translations should be reviewed by a speaker before release, as for any new label.
- [A microchip number typed onto the wrong pet blocks the right pet, and reception cannot see which pet holds it] → Accepted until the lookup ticket (D22, following from D5 and D11).

- **THEN** the form is shown again with "is already in use" on the name

### Requirement: Validation errors are reported together

The system SHALL report every validation error of a submission at once, in no particular order, including an error on the microchip number, and SHALL NOT save the pet while any error remains.

content.content:
1	# Decisions: pc-301
2	
3	Ticket: PC-301 Record a pet's microchip number
4	
5	## Decided
6	
7	- **D1** The term is **microchip number**. "Chip number", "chip ID" and "transponder" are not used. Asked as Q1, answered 2026-10-31.
8	- **D2** The microchip number is optional on both the add form and the edit form. Asked as Q2, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: required on both forms.
9	- **D3** A microchip number must be exactly 15 digits: ISO 11784 only. Asked as Q3, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: also accepting 9- or 10-character non-ISO chips (AVID, FDX-A).
10	- **D4** A microchip number is unique across all pets of all owners, not only within one owner. Asked as Q4, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: unique per owner.
11	- **D5** PC-301 only records the microchip number. Looking up a pet by its microchip number is a separate ticket. Asked as Q5, answered 2026-10-31.
12	- **D6** The owner's page shows each pet's microchip number with the pet's other details. Asked as Q6, answered 2026-10-31.
13	- **D7** The edit form accepts a new microchip number for a pet that already has one, under the same rules as adding. Asked as Q7, answered 2026-10-31.
14	- **D8** An empty microchip number on the edit form removes the stored number. The edit form must show the stored number, so clearing it is deliberate. Asked as Q8, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: an empty field keeps the old number.
15	- **D9** The entered value is trimmed and its spaces removed, then it must be exactly 15 digits. Only the digits are stored. Nothing else is removed (no dashes, no dots). Asked as Q9, answered 2026-10-31.
16	- **D10** A microchip number that is not 15 digits after D9 gets the error "must be 15 digits". A duplicate gets "is already in use". Both errors are on the microchip number field. Asked as Q10, answered 2026-10-31.
17	- **D11** The duplicate error is only "is already in use". The form must not show another owner's pet or details. Asked as Q11, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: naming the pet or owner that has the number.
18	- **D12** H2, MySQL and Postgres each get a named unique constraint on the microchip number. A duplicate caught by the database is reported as "is already in use" on the microchip number field. Where that code goes is a design decision, not part of this requirement. Asked as Q12, answered 2026-10-31.
19	- **D13** Fixing the unnamed MySQL pet-name constraint (F4) is not part of PC-301. It is a separate bug. Asked as Q13, answered 2026-10-31.
20	- **D14** A pet never conflicts with its own microchip number, compared after spaces are removed. Saving a pet again with the number it already has is accepted. Asked as Q14, answered 2026-10-31.
21	- **D15** Only the 15-digit check applies. The country or manufacturer code in the first three digits is not checked. Asked as Q15, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: checking against ISO 3166 numeric and manufacturer codes.
22	- **D16** On the owner's page, a pet without a microchip number shows the "Microchip number" label with an empty value. Asked as Q16, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: hiding the label; showing a word such as "none".
23	- **D17** A malformed microchip number gets the format error only. A well-formed duplicate gets "is already in use" only. Either one is reported together with the form's other errors. Asked as Q17, answered 2026-10-31.
24	- **D18** Where the uniqueness check lives in the code is a design decision for the change, not part of this requirement (see F6). Stated by the user on 2026-10-31.
25	- **D19** A duplicate caught by the database becomes the error on the microchip number field through a `PetValidator` method that rejects the field. The controller's `catch` calls that method. No new `rejectValue` call is added to a controller, and the freeze store stays as it is (F6, F11). Asked as G1 at the gate of 1 November, answered 2026-11-01. Rejected: one `rejectValue` call per `catch` that chooses the field (it reshapes the pinned name mapping); a waiver for two more frozen violations (it weakens the sensor); `@ControllerAdvice` (it avoids the rule instead of meeting it).
26	- **D20** *Replaced by D23 (G5, gate of 1 November, round 3); kept for the record.* PC-301 has no migration plan. Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are out of scope: the change covers the schema scripts the app starts from. No decision asked for a migration. Known gap recorded with this answer: the duplicate has no cross-database test. The MySQL and Postgres integration tests run only where Docker is available, and the change adds no microchip number test to them (Codex R3, left as it is). Asked as G2 at the gate of 1 November, answered 2026-11-01.

# database init, supports mysql too
database=h2
spring.sql.init.schema-locations=classpath*:db/${database}/schema.sql
spring.sql.init.data-locations=classpath*:db/${database}/data.sql

# Web
spring.thymeleaf.mode=HTML

# JPA
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false
spring.jpa.hibernate.naming.physical-strategy=org.hibernate.boot.model.naming.PhysicalNamingStrategySnakeCaseImpl
spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=16

# Internationalization
spring.messages.basename=messages/messages

# Actuator
# Expose all actuator endpoints for monitoring and management purposes
# Don't do this in production, only for development and testing
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=*

# Logging
logging.level.org.springframework=INFO
# logging.level.org.springframework.web=DEBUG
# logging.level.org.springframework.context.annotation=TRACE

# Maximum time static resources should be cached
spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.max-age=12h

services:
  mysql:
    image: mysql:9.7
    ports:
      - "3306:3306"
    environment:
      - MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=
      - MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=true
      - MYSQL_USER=petclinic
      - MYSQL_PASSWORD=petclinic
      - MYSQL_DATABASE=petclinic
    volumes:
      - "./conf.d:/etc/mysql/conf.d:ro"
  postgres:
    image: postgres:18.4
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=petclinic
      - POSTGRES_USER=petclinic
      - POSTGRES_DB=petclinic

# Tasks

Baseline: before starting, run `./mvnw test` and note any failures that already exist, so they are not blamed on this change.

The change ships in two releases, in this order (design Decision 8, D25): release 1 is section 0 alone; then the migration script runs; then release 2 is sections 1 to 6.

## 0. Release 1: column lists for the seed inserts

- [ ] 0.1 Give the pet inserts in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql` a column list (`id, name, birth_date, type_id, owner_id`), because they insert by position today (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`). Change nothing else: no schema change, no migration script, no microchip number. Leave `db/postgres/data.sql` unchanged: it already names its columns. Verify: the app starts on H2, `./mvnw test` passes with no failures beyond those noted at the baseline, and the release-1 diff touches only those two files. Where Docker is available, also run `MySqlIntegrationTests`; without Docker it is skipped, so report it as not run.
- [ ] 0.2 Release 1 is merged and released on its own, before any task of release 2 is merged. Deployment step 1 of design Decision 8 (release 1 deployed, no older instance left) must be done before the migration script runs on any database.

## Release 2: the microchip number

Deployment: run the migration script of task 1.5 after release 1 is deployed, then deploy release 2. Rollback from release 2 redeploys release 1, never the code before it (design Decision 8).

## 1. Schema and entity

- [ ] 1.1 Add the nullable `microchip_number` column and the constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` to `db/h2/schema.sql`, `db/mysql/schema.sql` and `db/postgres/schema.sql`, as in design Decisions 1 and 5. The seed inserts already name their columns (task 0.1). No seeded pet gets a microchip number (F8). Verify: the app starts on H2 and `./mvnw test -Dtest=ClinicServiceTests` passes.
- [ ] 1.2 Add `microchipNumber` to `Pet`, with the normalising setter from design Decision 2 (trim, remove spaces, empty becomes `null`). Verify: new unit tests in `PetTests` or `OwnerTests` show that `" 985 141 000 123 456 "` becomes `"985141000123456"`, that `"   "` and `""` become `null`, and that `"985-141-000-123-456"` is kept as it is. Run them with `./mvnw test -Dtest=OwnerTests` (or the new class).
- [ ] 1.3 Add `PetRepository` with `existsByMicrochipNumber` and `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot`. Verify: a test against H2 in `ClinicServiceTests` shows that both queries find another pet's number, that `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` does not find the pet's own number, and that two pets with no number can be saved. This covers the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number".
- [ ] 1.4 Add a deterministic test of the database duplicate on H2 to `ClinicServiceTests`, modelled on `shouldFailToInsertDuplicatePetNameForSameOwner` (`ClinicServiceTests.java:253-277`). It saves two pets, for different owners, with the same microchip number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so `PetValidator` does not run. It asserts that the save throws `DataIntegrityViolationException` and that the exception's message contains `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. This is the only test that reads H2's real message: the race test (task 4.2) may never reach the `catch` (design, Risks). Verify: `./mvnw test -Dtest=ClinicServiceTests` passes.
- [ ] 1.5 Add the migration scripts of design Decision 8 (D23): `src/main/resources/db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql` and `src/main/resources/db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`, each adding the nullable column first and the constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` second, with a leading comment that says to run it after release 1 is deployed and before release 2 is (D25). None for H2. Add one migration test per database, following the existing patterns and adding no dependency to `pom.xml` (D26, F13): the MySQL test uses a `testcontainers-mysql` container with `@Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true)`, as `MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43-49` does; the Postgres test starts Postgres through Spring Boot's Docker Compose support and skips itself without Docker, as `PostgresIntegrationTests.java:51-52,68` does. If either test cannot be written without a new dependency, stop and raise it with the ticket owner. Each test creates the `pets` table and the tables it references from the `schema.sql` of release 1 (the same as before this change), kept as a test resource, and inserts a pet. It then runs the migration script and checks that the existing pet has no microchip number, that two pets without a number can be saved, and that a second pet with the same number is rejected with an error that names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. Finally it runs the new `schema.sql` against the migrated database and checks that it succeeds, which is what step 3 of the deployment in Decision 8 relies on. Verify: with Docker, both tests pass. Without Docker they are skipped: report them as not run, not as passed (known gap, D23).

## 2. Validator rules

- [ ] 2.1 Give `PetValidator` a `PetRepository` constructor argument and add the format check `[0-9]{15}` with code `microchipNumber.invalid`. Verify: `PetValidatorTests` covers 15 digits accepted, `000000000000001` accepted, 14 and 16 digits rejected, `0A0139F53B` rejected, a dashed number rejected, and no number accepted. That is the spec requirements "Microchip number is optional", "is stored as its digits" and "is exactly 15 digits".
- [ ] 2.2 Add the uniqueness check with code `duplicate`. It runs only when the format check passes, with `existsByMicrochipNumber` for a new pet and `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` for an existing one. Verify: `PetValidatorTests`, with a mocked `PetRepository`, covers another pet's number rejected, the pet's own number accepted, and a malformed number that never reaches the repository and gets exactly one error. That is the spec requirements "unique across all pets", "A pet keeps its own microchip number" and "One microchip number error at a time".
- [ ] 2.3 Add `microchipNumber` and `microchipNumber.invalid` to `messages.properties` and every `messages_*.properties` except `messages_en`. Verify: `./mvnw test -Dtest=I18nPropertiesSyncTest` passes.

## 3. Pet forms

- [ ] 3.1 Inject `PetRepository` into `PetController` and build the validator with it in `initPetBinder`. Add `@MockitoBean PetRepository` to `PetControllerTests` and `PetControllerCharacterizationTests`. Verify: both classes pass unchanged otherwise, which shows the baseline `pets` behaviour still holds.
- [ ] 3.2 Copy `microchipNumber`, including `null`, in `updatePetDetails`. Verify: new `PetControllerTests` cases for "A new number replaces the stored one", "The field is cleared" and "Saving a pet with its own number" pass. Also check that the existing `editCopiesNameBirthDateAndTypeOntoOwnersPetWhenInstancesDiffer` still passes.
- [ ] 3.3 Add the microchip number input to `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html`. Verify: `PetControllerTests` asserts that the edit form for a pet with `985141000123456` holds that value and that a pet without a number shows an empty field. `./mvnw test -Dtest=I18nPropertiesSyncTest` still passes.
- [ ] 3.4 Verify in `PetControllerTests`:
  - the combined-error scenarios "Three errors on the add form, one on the microchip number" (with a valid type) and "Two errors on the edit form, one on the microchip number", including "is already in use" on the microchip number;
  - that the duplicate response for another owner's number contains neither the other pet's name nor the other owner's name;
  - "Editing a pet to another pet's number", with "petty" and "doggy" of the same owner;
  - "Spaces are removed" and "Fifteen digits are accepted" at the controller: the add form submitted with " 985 141 000 123 456 " and with "985141000123456" redirects, and the new pet on the owner passed to `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush` has the microchip number "985141000123456".
- [ ] 3.5 Add the G3 test (D21): one `@SpringBootTest` on H2 that goes through the forms. It adds a pet with "985141000123456", edits it to "985141000654321", then clears it. After each step it reads the stored value from the database: "985141000123456", then "985141000654321", then no number. It also submits an edit with "12345" for a pet that has a number, and checks that the form is shown again with "must be 15 digits" and that the stored value is unchanged. This covers "A new number replaces the stored one", "The field is cleared" and "A malformed new number is rejected" against a real database, and the detached-entity claim in design Decision 4. Verify: the test passes with `./mvnw test -Dtest=<the new class>`.

## 4. Duplicates caught by the database

- [ ] 4.1 Add the `PetValidator` method from design Decision 5 (D19), which rejects `microchipNumber` with the code `duplicate`. In both POST handlers, when a `DataIntegrityViolationException` names `unique_pet_microchip_number` (ignoring case), call that method before the name check and show the form again. Add no `rejectValue` call to `PetController`. Verify: a `PetValidatorTests` case shows that the method puts exactly one error, `duplicate`, on `microchipNumber`. New `PetControllerTests` cases for "The constraint is reported as a duplicate microchip number" and "The name constraint is still reported on the name" pass, and `createOtherIntegrityViolationIsRethrown` still passes (the MODIFIED scenario "Another integrity violation").
- [ ] 4.2 Add a race test for two simultaneous adds, for different owners, with the same microchip number to `PetClinicConcurrencyTests`, modelled on `testDuplicatePetNameRaceConditionIsBlocked`. Unlike that template, which counts any non-2xx response or exception as a failure (`PetClinicConcurrencyTests.java:86-95`), assert that the losing request gets the form again (status 200) with "is already in use" on the microchip number. Verify: exactly one pet with the number is saved on H2, and the losing response carries that error. The response is the same whether the validator or the database `catch` rejected the losing request, so this test does not show that H2's real message is recognised; task 1.4 does. Where Docker is available, also run `MySqlIntegrationTests` and `PostgresIntegrationTests`. If Docker is missing they are skipped, so report them as not run rather than as passed. They do not test the microchip constraint through the forms either way (known gap recorded with D20, design Risks).
- [ ] 4.3 Run `./mvnw test -Dtest=ArchitectureTests`. Verify: it passes with the freeze store unchanged. If it fails, do not edit or regenerate `src/test/resources/archunit_store/`. Stop and raise it with the ticket owner (design Decision 5).

## 5. Owner's page

- [ ] 5.1 Add the "Microchip number" label and value to `owners/ownerDetails.html`, after the type. Verify: `OwnerControllerTests` asserts the label with `985141000123456` for a pet with a number, and the label with an empty value (not "none") for a pet without one. That is the spec `owner-details`.

## 6. Integration check

- [ ] 6.1 Run `./mvnw spring-javaformat:apply` and then the full `./mvnw test`. Verify: the build passes, and no failures appear beyond those noted at the baseline.
- [ ] 6.2 Run `openspec validate pc-301 --strict`. Verify: it reports the change as valid.

## Workflow follow-up

- When archiving, update the Purpose of `openspec/specs/pets/spec.md`. It says the spec does not cover the GET forms, but the requirement "The edit form shows the stored microchip number" is a GET-form behaviour.
- Open the two follow-up tickets from `decisions.md`: looking up a pet by its microchip number (D5), and the unnamed MySQL owner-and-pet-name constraint (D13, F4). The lookup ticket should name the wrong-pet case accepted in D22 as something it fixes, and list the microchip number on the visit form (`templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html`), which this change leaves out (D24).

# Tasks

Baseline: before starting, run `./mvnw test` and note any failures that already exist, so they are not blamed on this change.

The change ships in two releases, in this order (design Decision 8, D25): release 1 is section 0 alone; then the migration script runs; then release 2 is sections 1 to 6.

## 0. Release 1: column lists for the seed inserts

- [x] 0.1 Give the pet inserts in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql` a column list (`id, name, birth_date, type_id, owner_id`), because they insert by position today (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`). Change nothing else: no schema change, no migration script, no microchip number. Leave `db/postgres/data.sql` unchanged: it already names its columns. Verify: the app starts on H2, `./mvnw test` passes with no failures beyond those noted at the baseline, and the release-1 diff touches only those two files. Where Docker is available, also run `MySqlIntegrationTests`; without Docker it is skipped, so report it as not run.
- [ ] 0.2 Release 1 is merged and released on its own, before any task of release 2 is merged. Deployment step 1 of design Decision 8 (release 1 deployed, no older instance left) must be done before the migration script runs on any database.

## Release 2: the microchip number

Deployment: run the migration script of task 1.5 after release 1 is deployed, then deploy release 2. Rollback from release 2 redeploys release 1, never the code before it (design Decision 8).

## 1. Schema and entity

- [ ] 1.1 Add the nullable `microchip_number` column and the constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` to `db/h2/schema.sql`, `db/mysql/schema.sql` and `db/postgres/schema.sql`, as in design Decisions 1 and 5. The seed inserts already name their columns (task 0.1). No seeded pet gets a microchip number (F8). Verify: the app starts on H2 and `./mvnw test -Dtest=ClinicServiceTests` passes.
- [ ] 1.2 Add `microchipNumber` to `Pet`, with the normalising setter from design Decision 2 (trim, remove spaces, empty becomes `null`). Verify: new unit tests in `PetTests` or `OwnerTests` show that `" 985 141 000 123 456 "` becomes `"985141000123456"`, that `"   "` and `""` become `null`, and that `"985-141-000-123-456"` is kept as it is. Run them with `./mvnw test -Dtest=OwnerTests` (or the new class).
- [ ] 1.3 Add `PetRepository` with `existsByMicrochipNumber` and `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot`. Verify: a test against H2 in `ClinicServiceTests` shows that both queries find another pet's number, that `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` does not find the pet's own number, and that two pets with no number can be saved. This covers the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number".
- [ ] 1.4 Add a deterministic test of the database duplicate on H2 to `ClinicServiceTests`, modelled on `shouldFailToInsertDuplicatePetNameForSameOwner` (`ClinicServiceTests.java:253-277`). It saves two pets, for different owners, with the same microchip number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so `PetValidator` does not run. It asserts that the save throws `DataIntegrityViolationException` and that the exception's message contains `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. This is the only test that reads H2's real message: the race test (task 4.2) may never reach the `catch` (design, Risks). Verify: `./mvnw test -Dtest=ClinicServiceTests` passes.
- [ ] 1.5 Add the migration scripts of design Decision 8 (D23): `src/main/resources/db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql` and `src/main/resources/db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`, each adding the nullable column first and the constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` second, with a leading comment that says to run it after release 1 is deployed and before release 2 is (D25). None for H2. Add one migration test per database, following the existing patterns and adding no dependency to `pom.xml` (D26, F13): the MySQL test uses a `testcontainers-mysql` container with `@Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true)`, as `MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43-49` does; the Postgres test starts Postgres through Spring Boot's Docker Compose support and skips itself without Docker, as `PostgresIntegrationTests.java:51-52,68` does. If either test cannot be written without a new dependency, stop and raise it with the ticket owner. Each test creates the `pets` table and the tables it references from the `schema.sql` of release 1 (the same as before this change), kept as a test resource, and inserts a pet. It then runs the migration script and checks that the existing pet has no microchip number, that two pets without a number can be saved, and that a second pet with the same number is rejected with an error that names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. Finally it runs the new `schema.sql` against the migrated database and checks that it succeeds, which is what step 3 of the deployment in Decision 8 relies on. Verify: with Docker, both tests pass. Without Docker they are skipped: report them as not run, not as passed (known gap, D23).

## 2. Validator rules

- [ ] 2.1 Give `PetValidator` a `PetRepository` constructor argument and add the format check `[0-9]{15}` with code `microchipNumber.invalid`. Verify: `PetValidatorTests` covers 15 digits accepted, `000000000000001` accepted, 14 and 16 digits rejected, `0A0139F53B` rejected, a dashed number rejected, and no number accepted. That is the spec requirements "Microchip number is optional", "is stored as its digits" and "is exactly 15 digits".
- [ ] 2.2 Add the uniqueness check with code `duplicate`. It runs only when the format check passes, with `existsByMicrochipNumber` for a new pet and `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` for an existing one. Verify: `PetValidatorTests`, with a mocked `PetRepository`, covers another pet's number rejected, the pet's own number accepted, and a malformed number that never reaches the repository and gets exactly one error. That is the spec requirements "unique across all pets", "A pet keeps its own microchip number" and "One microchip number error at a time".
- [ ] 2.3 Add `microchipNumber` and `microchipNumber.invalid` to `messages.properties` and every `messages_*.properties` except `messages_en`. Verify: `./mvnw test -Dtest=I18nPropertiesSyncTest` passes.

## 3. Pet forms

- [ ] 3.1 Inject `PetRepository` into `PetController` and build the validator with it in `initPetBinder`. Add `@MockitoBean PetRepository` to `PetControllerTests` and `PetControllerCharacterizationTests`. Verify: both classes pass unchanged otherwise, which shows the baseline `pets` behaviour still holds.
- [ ] 3.2 Copy `microchipNumber`, including `null`, in `updatePetDetails`. Verify: new `PetControllerTests` cases for "A new number replaces the stored one", "The field is cleared" and "Saving a pet with its own number" pass. Also check that the existing `editCopiesNameBirthDateAndTypeOntoOwnersPetWhenInstancesDiffer` still passes.
- [ ] 3.3 Add the microchip number input to `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html`. Verify: `PetControllerTests` asserts that the edit form for a pet with `985141000123456` holds that value and that a pet without a number shows an empty field. `./mvnw test -Dtest=I18nPropertiesSyncTest` still passes.
- [ ] 3.4 Verify in `PetControllerTests`:
  - the combined-error scenarios "Three errors on the add form, one on the microchip number" (with a valid type) and "Two errors on the edit form, one on the microchip number", including "is already in use" on the microchip number;
  - that the duplicate response for another owner's number contains neither the other pet's name nor the other owner's name;
  - "Editing a pet to another pet's number", with "petty" and "doggy" of the same owner;
  - "Spaces are removed" and "Fifteen digits are accepted" at the controller: the add form submitted with " 985 141 000 123 456 " and with "985141000123456" redirects, and the new pet on the owner passed to `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush` has the microchip number "985141000123456".
- [ ] 3.5 Add the G3 test (D21): one `@SpringBootTest` on H2 that goes through the forms. It adds a pet with "985141000123456", edits it to "985141000654321", then clears it. After each step it reads the stored value from the database: "985141000123456", then "985141000654321", then no number. It also submits an edit with "12345" for a pet that has a number, and checks that the form is shown again with "must be 15 digits" and that the stored value is unchanged. This covers "A new number replaces the stored one", "The field is cleared" and "A malformed new number is rejected" against a real database, and the detached-entity claim in design Decision 4. Verify: the test passes with `./mvnw test -Dtest=<the new class>`.

## 4. Duplicates caught by the database

- [ ] 4.1 Add the `PetValidator` method from design Decision 5 (D19), which rejects `microchipNumber` with the code `duplicate`. In both POST handlers, when a `DataIntegrityViolationException` names `unique_pet_microchip_number` (ignoring case), call that method before the name check and show the form again. Add no `rejectValue` call to `PetController`. Verify: a `PetValidatorTests` case shows that the method puts exactly one error, `duplicate`, on `microchipNumber`. New `PetControllerTests` cases for "The constraint is reported as a duplicate microchip number" and "The name constraint is still reported on the name" pass, and `createOtherIntegrityViolationIsRethrown` still passes (the MODIFIED scenario "Another integrity violation").
- [ ] 4.2 Add a race test for two simultaneous adds, for different owners, with the same microchip number to `PetClinicConcurrencyTests`, modelled on `testDuplicatePetNameRaceConditionIsBlocked`. Unlike that template, which counts any non-2xx response or exception as a failure (`PetClinicConcurrencyTests.java:86-95`), assert that the losing request gets the form again (status 200) with "is already in use" on the microchip number. Verify: exactly one pet with the number is saved on H2, and the losing response carries that error. The response is the same whether the validator or the database `catch` rejected the losing request, so this test does not show that H2's real message is recognised; task 1.4 does. Where Docker is available, also run `MySqlIntegrationTests` and `PostgresIntegrationTests`. If Docker is missing they are skipped, so report them as not run rather than as passed. They do not test the microchip constraint through the forms either way (known gap recorded with D20, design Risks).
- [ ] 4.3 Run `./mvnw test -Dtest=ArchitectureTests`. Verify: it passes with the freeze store unchanged. If it fails, do not edit or regenerate `src/test/resources/archunit_store/`. Stop and raise it with the ticket owner (design Decision 5).

## 5. Owner's page

- [ ] 5.1 Add the "Microchip number" label and value to `owners/ownerDetails.html`, after the type. Verify: `OwnerControllerTests` asserts the label with `985141000123456` for a pet with a number, and the label with an empty value (not "none") for a pet without one. That is the spec `owner-details`.

## 6. Integration check

- [ ] 6.1 Run `./mvnw spring-javaformat:apply` and then the full `./mvnw test`. Verify: the build passes, and no failures appear beyond those noted at the baseline.
- [ ] 6.2 Run `openspec validate pc-301 --strict`. Verify: it reports the change as valid.

## Workflow follow-up

- When archiving, update the Purpose of `openspec/specs/pets/spec.md`. It says the spec does not cover the GET forms, but the requirement "The edit form shows the stored microchip number" is a GET-form behaviour.
- Open the two follow-up tickets from `decisions.md`: looking up a pet by its microchip number (D5), and the unnamed MySQL owner-and-pet-name constraint (D13, F4). The lookup ticket should name the wrong-pet case accepted in D22 as something it fixes, and list the microchip number on the visit form (`templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html`), which this change leaves out (D24).

# Tasks

Baseline: before starting, run `./mvnw test` and note any failures that already exist, so they are not blamed on this change.

The change ships in two releases, in this order (design Decision 8, D25): release 1 is section 0 alone; then the migration script runs; then release 2 is sections 1 to 6.

## 0. Release 1: column lists for the seed inserts

- [x] 0.1 Give the pet inserts in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql` a column list (`id, name, birth_date, type_id, owner_id`), because they insert by position today (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`). Change nothing else: no schema change, no migration script, no microchip number. Leave `db/postgres/data.sql` unchanged: it already names its columns. Verify: the app starts on H2, `./mvnw test` passes with no failures beyond those noted at the baseline, and the release-1 diff touches only those two files. Where Docker is available, also run `MySqlIntegrationTests`; without Docker it is skipped, so report it as not run.
- [ ] 0.2 Release 1 is merged and released on its own, before any task of release 2 is merged. Deployment step 1 of design Decision 8 (release 1 deployed, no older instance left) must be done before the migration script runs on any database.

## Release 2: the microchip number

Deployment: run the migration script of task 1.5 after release 1 is deployed, then deploy release 2. Rollback from release 2 redeploys release 1, never the code before it (design Decision 8).

## 1. Schema and entity

- [x] 1.1 Add the nullable `microchip_number` column and the constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` to `db/h2/schema.sql`, `db/mysql/schema.sql` and `db/postgres/schema.sql`, as in design Decisions 1 and 5. The seed inserts already name their columns (task 0.1). No seeded pet gets a microchip number (F8). Verify: the app starts on H2 and `./mvnw test -Dtest=ClinicServiceTests` passes.
- [x] 1.2 Add `microchipNumber` to `Pet`, with the normalising setter from design Decision 2 (trim, remove spaces, empty becomes `null`). Verify: new unit tests in `PetTests` or `OwnerTests` show that `" 985 141 000 123 456 "` becomes `"985141000123456"`, that `"   "` and `""` become `null`, and that `"985-141-000-123-456"` is kept as it is. Run them with `./mvnw test -Dtest=OwnerTests` (or the new class).
- [x] 1.3 Add `PetRepository` with `existsByMicrochipNumber` and `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot`. Verify: a test against H2 in `ClinicServiceTests` shows that both queries find another pet's number, that `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` does not find the pet's own number, and that two pets with no number can be saved. This covers the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number".
- [x] 1.4 Add a deterministic test of the database duplicate on H2 to `ClinicServiceTests`, modelled on `shouldFailToInsertDuplicatePetNameForSameOwner` (`ClinicServiceTests.java:253-277`). It saves two pets, for different owners, with the same microchip number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so `PetValidator` does not run. It asserts that the save throws `DataIntegrityViolationException` and that the exception's message contains `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. This is the only test that reads H2's real message: the race test (task 4.2) may never reach the `catch` (design, Risks). Verify: `./mvnw test -Dtest=ClinicServiceTests` passes.
- [ ] 1.5 Add the migration scripts of design Decision 8 (D23): `src/main/resources/db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql` and `src/main/resources/db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`, each adding the nullable column first and the constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` second, with a leading comment that says to run it after release 1 is deployed and before release 2 is (D25). None for H2. Add one migration test per database, following the existing patterns and adding no dependency to `pom.xml` (D26, F13): the MySQL test uses a `testcontainers-mysql` container with `@Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true)`, as `MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43-49` does; the Postgres test starts Postgres through Spring Boot's Docker Compose support and skips itself without Docker, as `PostgresIntegrationTests.java:51-52,68` does. If either test cannot be written without a new dependency, stop and raise it with the ticket owner. Each test creates the `pets` table and the tables it references from the `schema.sql` of release 1 (the same as before this change), kept as a test resource, and inserts a pet. It then runs the migration script and checks that the existing pet has no microchip number, that two pets without a number can be saved, and that a second pet with the same number is rejected with an error that names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. Finally it runs the new `schema.sql` against the migrated database and checks that it succeeds, which is what step 3 of the deployment in Decision 8 relies on. Verify: with Docker, both tests pass. Without Docker they are skipped: report them as not run, not as passed (known gap, D23).

## 2. Validator rules

- [ ] 2.1 Give `PetValidator` a `PetRepository` constructor argument and add the format check `[0-9]{15}` with code `microchipNumber.invalid`. Verify: `PetValidatorTests` covers 15 digits accepted, `000000000000001` accepted, 14 and 16 digits rejected, `0A0139F53B` rejected, a dashed number rejected, and no number accepted. That is the spec requirements "Microchip number is optional", "is stored as its digits" and "is exactly 15 digits".
- [ ] 2.2 Add the uniqueness check with code `duplicate`. It runs only when the format check passes, with `existsByMicrochipNumber` for a new pet and `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` for an existing one. Verify: `PetValidatorTests`, with a mocked `PetRepository`, covers another pet's number rejected, the pet's own number accepted, and a malformed number that never reaches the repository and gets exactly one error. That is the spec requirements "unique across all pets", "A pet keeps its own microchip number" and "One microchip number error at a time".
- [ ] 2.3 Add `microchipNumber` and `microchipNumber.invalid` to `messages.properties` and every `messages_*.properties` except `messages_en`. Verify: `./mvnw test -Dtest=I18nPropertiesSyncTest` passes.

## 3. Pet forms

- [ ] 3.1 Inject `PetRepository` into `PetController` and build the validator with it in `initPetBinder`. Add `@MockitoBean PetRepository` to `PetControllerTests` and `PetControllerCharacterizationTests`. Verify: both classes pass unchanged otherwise, which shows the baseline `pets` behaviour still holds.
- [ ] 3.2 Copy `microchipNumber`, including `null`, in `updatePetDetails`. Verify: new `PetControllerTests` cases for "A new number replaces the stored one", "The field is cleared" and "Saving a pet with its own number" pass. Also check that the existing `editCopiesNameBirthDateAndTypeOntoOwnersPetWhenInstancesDiffer` still passes.
- [ ] 3.3 Add the microchip number input to `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html`. Verify: `PetControllerTests` asserts that the edit form for a pet with `985141000123456` holds that value and that a pet without a number shows an empty field. `./mvnw test -Dtest=I18nPropertiesSyncTest` still passes.
- [ ] 3.4 Verify in `PetControllerTests`:
  - the combined-error scenarios "Three errors on the add form, one on the microchip number" (with a valid type) and "Two errors on the edit form, one on the microchip number", including "is already in use" on the microchip number;
  - that the duplicate response for another owner's number contains neither the other pet's name nor the other owner's name;
  - "Editing a pet to another pet's number", with "petty" and "doggy" of the same owner;
  - "Spaces are removed" and "Fifteen digits are accepted" at the controller: the add form submitted with " 985 141 000 123 456 " and with "985141000123456" redirects, and the new pet on the owner passed to `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush` has the microchip number "985141000123456".
- [ ] 3.5 Add the G3 test (D21): one `@SpringBootTest` on H2 that goes through the forms. It adds a pet with "985141000123456", edits it to "985141000654321", then clears it. tool_use_result.originalFile:
# Tasks

Baseline: before starting, run `./mvnw test` and note any failures that already exist, so they are not blamed on this change.

The change ships in two releases, in this order (design Decision 8, D25): release 1 is section 0 alone; then the migration script runs; then release 2 is sections 1 to 6.

## 0. Release 1: column lists for the seed inserts

- [x] 0.1 Give the pet inserts in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql` a column list (`id, name, birth_date, type_id, owner_id`), because they insert by position today (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`). Change nothing else: no schema change, no migration script, no microchip number. Leave `db/postgres/data.sql` unchanged: it already names its columns. Verify: the app starts on H2, `./mvnw test` passes with no failures beyond those noted at the baseline, and the release-1 diff touches only those two files. Where Docker is available, also run `MySqlIntegrationTests`; without Docker it is skipped, so report it as not run.
- [ ] 0.2 Release 1 is merged and released on its own, before any task of release 2 is merged. Deployment step 1 of design Decision 8 (release 1 deployed, no older instance left) must be done before the migration script runs on any database.

## Release 2: the microchip number

Deployment: run the migration script of task 1.5 after release 1 is deployed, then deploy release 2. Rollback from release 2 redeploys release 1, never the code before it (design Decision 8).

## 1. Schema and entity

- [x] 1.1 Add the nullable `microchip_number` column and the constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` to `db/h2/schema.sql`, `db/mysql/schema.sql` and `db/postgres/schema.sql`, as in design Decisions 1 and 5. The seed inserts already name their columns (task 0.1). No seeded pet gets a microchip number (F8). Verify: the app starts on H2 and `./mvnw test -Dtest=ClinicServiceTests` passes.
- [x] 1.2 Add `microchipNumber` to `Pet`, with the normalising setter from design Decision 2 (trim, remove spaces, empty becomes `null`). Verify: new unit tests in `PetTests` or `OwnerTests` show that `" 985 141 000 123 456 "` becomes `"985141000123456"`, that `"   "` and `""` become `null`, and that `"985-141-000-123-456"` is kept as it is. Run them with `./mvnw test -Dtest=OwnerTests` (or the new class).
- [x] 1.3 Add `PetRepository` with `existsByMicrochipNumber` and `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot`. Verify: a test against H2 in `ClinicServiceTests` shows that both queries find another pet's number, that `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` does not find the pet's own number, and that two pets with no number can be saved. This covers the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number".
- [x] 1.4 Add a deterministic test of the database duplicate on H2 to `ClinicServiceTests`, modelled on `shouldFailToInsertDuplicatePetNameForSameOwner` (`ClinicServiceTests.java:253-277`). It saves two pets, for different owners, with the same microchip number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so `PetValidator` does not run. Baseline: before starting, run `./mvnw test` and note any failures that already exist, so they are not blamed on this change.

## 0. Release 1: column lists for the seed inserts

Change nothing else: no schema change, no migration script, no microchip number. Leave `db/postgres/data.sql` unchanged: it already names its columns. Verify: the app starts on H2, `./mvnw test` passes with no failures beyond those noted at the baseline, and the release-1 diff touches only those two files. Where Docker is available, also run `MySqlIntegrationTests`; without Docker it is skipped, so report it as not run.
- [ ] 0.2 Release 1 is merged and released on its own, before any task of release 2 is merged. Deployment step 1 of design Decision 8 (release 1 deployed, no older instance left) must be done before the migration script runs on any database.

Verify: a test against H2 in `ClinicServiceTests` shows that both queries find another pet's number, that `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` does not find the pet's own number, and that two pets with no number can be saved. This covers the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number".

It saves two pets, for different owners, with the same microchip number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so `PetValidator` does not run. It asserts that the save throws `DataIntegrityViolationException` and that the exception's message contains `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. This is the only test that reads H2's real message: the race test (task 4.2) may never reach the `catch` (design, Risks). Verify: `./mvnw test -Dtest=ClinicServiceTests` passes.
- [ ] 1.5 Add the migration scripts of design Decision 8 (D23): `src/main/resources/db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql` and `src/main/resources/db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`, each adding the nullable column first and the constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` second, with a leading comment that says to run it after release 1 is deployed and before release 2 is (D25). If either test cannot be written without a new dependency, stop and raise it with the ticket owner. Each test creates the `pets` table and the tables it references from the `schema.sql` of release 1 (the same as before this change), kept as a test resource, and inserts a pet. It then runs the migration script and checks that the existing pet has no microchip number, that two pets without a number can be saved, and that a second pet with the same number is rejected with an error that names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. Finally it runs the new `schema.sql` against the migrated database and checks that it succeeds, which is what step 3 of the deployment in Decision 8 relies on. Verify: with Docker, both tests pass. Without Docker they are skipped: report them as not run, not as passed (known gap, D23).

- [x] 2.1 Give `PetValidator` a `PetRepository` constructor argument and add the format check `[0-9]{15}` with code `microchipNumber.invalid`. Verify: `PetValidatorTests` covers 15 digits accepted, `000000000000001` accepted, 14 and 16 digits rejected, `0A0139F53B` rejected, a dashed number rejected, and no number accepted. That is the spec requirements "Microchip number is optional", "is stored as its digits" and "is exactly 15 digits".
- [x] 2.2 Add the uniqueness check with code `duplicate`. It runs only when the format check passes, with `existsByMicrochipNumber` for a new pet and `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot` for an existing one. Verify: `PetValidatorTests`, with a mocked `PetRepository`, covers another pet's number rejected, the pet's own number accepted, and a malformed number that never reaches the repository and gets exactly one error. - [x] 3.1 Inject `PetRepository` into `PetController` and build the validator with it in `initPetBinder`. Add `@MockitoBean PetRepository` to `PetControllerTests` and `PetControllerCharacterizationTests`. Verify: both classes pass unchanged otherwise, which shows the baseline `pets` behaviour still holds.
- [ ] 3.2 Copy `microchipNumber`, including `null`, in `updatePetDetails`. Verify: new `PetControllerTests` cases for "A new number replaces the stored one", "The field is cleared" and "Saving a pet with its own number" pass. - [ ] 3.3 Add the microchip number input to `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html`. Verify: `PetControllerTests` asserts that the edit form for a pet with `985141000123456` holds that value and that a pet without a number shows an empty field. `./mvnw test -Dtest=I18nPropertiesSyncTest` still passes.
- [ ] 3.4 Verify in `PetControllerTests`:
  - the combined-error scenarios "Three errors on the add form, one on the microchip number" (with a valid type) and "Two errors on the edit form, one on the microchip number", including "is already in use" on the microchip number;
